name: Elizabeth Blackburn
description: Elizabeth Blackburn discovered telomerase — the enzyme that replenishes the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes — work for which she shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Carol Greider and Jack Szostak. Her research established that telomere shortening is a molecular clock of cellular aging and linked telomere dysfunction to cancer, cardiovascular disease, and age-related conditions. Blackburn served as President of the Salk Institute for Biological Studies and was controversially removed from the President's Council on Bioethics in 2004 for dissenting from stem-cell research restrictions. Her collaboration with health psychologist Elissa Epel showed that chronic psychological stress accelerates telomere shortening in caregivers, opening an entirely new psycho-biological research field. She holds foundational patents underlying telomerase-targeted cancer therapies in clinical development at multiple biotechnology companies.
